purpose: Explanatory subject regions and thematic cross-references for the included roadmap snapshot.

foundations.description: The shared constructions used throughout the atlas: schemes and stacks, derived sheaves, commutative algebra, homotopy theory and general K-theory. These roadmaps live together because they supply definitions and theorems used across several areas; specialized arithmetic constructions have their own homes.

classical.description: Integers, primes, number fields and explicit calculation, studied through analytic estimates, algebraic structure and counting. This region joins classical arithmetic to modern sieve methods, additive combinatorics, arithmetic statistics and certified algorithms; several routes lead into geometry, modular forms and cohomology.
topics: Prime distribution, zeta functions and sieves

diophantine.description: Arithmetic questions about geometric objects: rational points, abelian varieties, moduli, heights and reduction. The common thread is using geometry to understand solutions of equations, including effective methods, finiteness theorems and arithmetic fundamental groups.

modular.description: The connections between modular forms, Shimura varieties and Galois representations. Roadmaps here assemble geometric towers, Hecke actions, p-adic families and deformation methods toward precisely stated modularity and automorphy results; the region has strong ties to cohomology and Iwasawa theory.
topics: Modular forms, modular curves and Hecke theory

automorphic.description: The general theory of automorphic forms on reductive groups, built from local representations, adelic quotients and spectral analysis. This is the common setting used by the more specialized modular, Langlands and arithmetic special-value roadmaps.
topics: Adeles, reductive groups and arithmetic quotients
Automorphic forms and locally symmetric spaces

diamonds.description: Geometric structures used to approach local Langlands through the Fargues–Fontaine curve: diamonds, v-stacks, bundles and sheaf categories. The roadmaps build from local geometry toward Hecke correspondences, geometric Satake and spectral actions, with explicit coefficient and group hypotheses.
topics: Vector bundles, isocrystals and Newton strata

cohomology.description: Cohomology theories and nonarchimedean spaces that translate geometry into arithmetic invariants. Étale, crystalline, de Rham and prismatic constructions sit alongside comparison theorems, weights and p-adic Hodge theory; adic, perfectoid and Berkovich geometry provide their geometric settings.
topics: Étale cohomology, duality and perverse sheaves
Crystalline and derived de Rham cohomology
Weights, purity and the Weil conjectures

motivic.description: Algebraic K-theory, motives and regulators connect cycles and arithmetic to periods and special values of L-functions. The Habiro branch adds cyclotomic completions, arithmetic q-series and quantum-topological invariants. General-purpose foundations are separated from these arithmetic applications.
topics: K-theory of fields, rings and schemes
Symbols, Bloch groups and explicit regulators
Arithmetic quantum topology and trace methods

iwasawa.description: Arithmetic in p-adic towers, organized around Selmer groups, p-adic L-functions and Euler systems. These roadmaps relate analytic interpolation to Galois cohomology and descent, leading to specific main-conjecture and rank-zero or rank-one BSD targets with their stated hypotheses.
topics: Heegner points, cycles and height formulas
Main conjectures and rank-zero or rank-one BSD

functionfields.description: Arithmetic over function fields, together with higher-dimensional local arithmetic. Drinfeld modules, t-motives and global shtukas form characteristic-p counterparts to several number-field themes; higher local fields have their own reciprocity and class-field-theoretic constructions.

analysis.description: Tau Ceti’s analysis roadmaps range from holomorphic functions and Hilbert-space expansions to probability, transport and partial differential equations. They share analytic constructions and estimates while retaining distinct endpoints, including de Finetti, semigroup and geometric function theory.

topology.description: The topology of spaces and manifolds, with covering spaces, geometric topology and both analytic and combinatorial Heegaard Floer theory. These roadmaps are grouped by their geometric objects and invariants; the separate homotopy foundations for K-theory also provide a useful thematic connection.

algebra.description: Groups, algebras and their representations, from finite-group character tables to Lie groups, highest weights and reductive algebraic groups. The representation-theory collection contains linked subroadmaps; this region supplies algebraic structures used across automorphic and geometric arithmetic.
topics: Reductive groups, Clifford algebras and spin representations

StableHomotopyKTheory.reason: Homotopy fibres, group completion and spectra are constructed for algebraic K-theory.

EnhancedDerivedSheaves.reason: Enhanced sheaf categories and coherent operations support the cohomology roadmaps.

DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra.reason: The algebraic infrastructure is used by Galois deformation and modularity-lifting arguments.

GeneralAlgebraicKTheory.reason: General constructions supply the arithmetic K-theory and regulator applications.

ArithmeticStatistics.reason: Counting families is organized by heights and includes geometric parametrizations and Selmer distributions.

DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence.reason: Height estimates and approximation theorems supply rational-point and effective Diophantine methods.

LogicAndDefinabilityInNumberTheory.reason: The roadmap explicitly includes motivic integration and transfer alongside valued-field logic.

QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms.reason: Theta, Jacobi and mock modular forms meet Habiro completions and arithmetic q-series.

FiniteFieldsAndCharacterSums.reason: Its Weil–Deligne bounds and point-counting stages use cohomological inputs.

ComplexComparisonPartII.reason: Coherent GAGA and de Rham comparison are geometric comparison constructions used by arithmetic moduli.

FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeThe.reason: Integral local Hodge theory links finite flat groups to Galois deformation rings and modularity applications.

ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciproc.reason: The roadmap explicitly consumes Shimura-variety CM reciprocity and constructs CM Galois realizations.

TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic.reason: Skeletons, divisors and specialization provide tools for arithmetic curves and dynamics.

ArithmeticQuantumTopology.reason: Framed links, surgery and quantum invariants connect Habiro rings to arithmetic q-series.

HabiroNahmSeries.reason: Nahm-series asymptotics and Bloch classes meet modular functions and arithmetic q-series.

BorelRegulators.reason: Arithmetic-group and relative Lie-algebra cohomology construct regulator classes.

PadicHodgeRegulators.reason: Local p-adic comparison, Bloch–Kato exponentials and Perrin–Riou interpolation connect regulators to Iwasawa cohomology.

GeneralizedHeegnerCycles.reason: Higher-dimensional cycles on modular geometry yield Abel–Jacobi classes and Euler systems.

GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights.reason: Arithmetic intersection and point-height formulas are compared with toric periods and automorphic L-values.

RankZeroOneBSD.reason: The targets concern elliptic-curve ranks and Tate–Shafarevich finiteness, using modularity and arithmetic descent.

PadicFamilies.reason: Hida and Coleman families include p-adic L-functions and arithmetic specializations.

PerfectoidShimuraVarieties.reason: Shimura towers are realized using perfectoid geometry and Hodge–Tate period maps.

HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups.reason: Relative p-adic comparison and integral period constructions feed automorphic geometry.

ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces.reason: Topological cohomology, local systems and Borel–Serre boundaries are constructed for arithmetic quotients.

MetaplecticAutomorphicForms.reason: Weil representations and dual pairs supply theta kernels and half-integral-weight forms.

GeometricSatakeAndFusion.reason: Sheaf convolution and fusion recover the dual reductive group through a representation-theoretic equivalence.

HeckeStacksAndLocalShtukas.reason: Local shtuka cohomology is built as a representation-valued functor with commuting actions.

WeilConjectures.reason: Cohomological zeta functions control finite-field point counts, including curves over finite fields.

GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands.reason: Global shtuka cohomology links function-field automorphic data to Galois parameters.

notes: Each roadmap has one primary region in atlas.json. Secondary tags describe mathematical themes; they are not additional dependency edges or completion claims.

bridgeGroups lists up to three other regions with the most recorded cross-region roadmap edges, counting both directions. It describes connections in this snapshot, not mathematical similarity or prerequisite order.
The 13 regions organize the included roadmaps rather than claiming an exhaustive taxonomy of mathematics.

Several primary homes intentionally follow the application: ComplexComparisonPartII and finite flat p-adic Hodge theory sit with arithmetic geometry; perfectoid Shimura towers sit with modular theory. Secondary tags make those methodological overlaps visible.
Arithmetic quantum topology has a motivic home because its current roadmap develops Habiro and regulator interfaces; the topology tag also exposes its link and three-manifold content.
The diamonds region concerns the Fargues–Fontaine/local-Langlands route. Global shtukas over function fields retain their separate function-field home.
General representation theory is a collection with child roadmaps. The metadata does not turn parent–child membership into a prerequisite.
